_comment: Gold star: which postings are worth a hand-curated resume.
A star does NOT mean 'good job'. It means high marginal return on spending
30-60 minutes tailoring a resume -- P(curation flips the decision) x value
of the job. Company prestige and pay are only the second factor.
WHY THIS LIVES IN web/lib/ RATHER THAN fixtures/: Vercel is configured with
web/ as the deployment root (see README), so anything outside web/ is not in
the bundle -- an import of ../../fixtures/ would build locally and fail in
production. Python has no such constraint: GitHub Actions checks out the
whole repo, so scraper/gold_star.py reads across into web/lib/ instead. The
constrained side holds the file; the unconstrained side reaches for it.
SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for two implementations: web/lib/goldStar.ts drives
the dashboard, scraper/gold_star.py drives the ntfy push. Two copies of one
rule drift silently -- that is exactly what fixtures/canonical_target_keys
.json exists to prevent for target_key -- so the data AND the parity cases
live here, and BOTH test suites assert every entry in `cases`. Change the
rule in one language without the other and a test goes red in both.
TUNING: this file is the dial. Editing it needs no migration, no backfill
and no reclassification -- the star is derived at render/push time, never
stored. Run scraper/count_stars.py after any edit: if more than ~5% of To
apply is starred, the star is wallpaper and the thresholds are too loose.
companies: matched AFTER norm_company-style normalisation (lowercase, strip
punctuation/YC tags/leading 'the', drop noise words like inc/corp/labs), so
'Regions' and 'Regions Bank' collapse together and cannot slip past. Write
them here in readable form; normalisation happens in code.
The MEDIAN of a stated band must clear these (changed 2026-09-11). It
was the lower bound, to stop a high ceiling creating false stars -- but
that also sank every wide band whatever its midpoint, and a wide band is
how the best-paying employers post. '$20 - $70/hr' is a $45/hr job.
35/hr x 2080 hours = 72,800/yr, so the two thresholds describe the same
pay rather than two different bars. Change them together or a posting
will star or not depending only on which unit it happened to quote.
Set from the candidate's own stated line: anything paying $35+/hr is
worth a curated resume. Previously 45/90k, which was a guess and which
missed Wells Fargo despite it stating a salary.
